metadata.title: Testing My Judge for Bias
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week06/term2-week6-video-content.md (Week 6); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: don't guess about judge bias, test it blind — GPT-4o-mini showed no self-preference; it is generally lenient. Credit: the conflict-of-interest critique came from the reviewer; the experiment, script and paper rewrite are Janvi's. Only Professor Brown may be named. Every on-screen number appears in the Week 6 source as written.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about testing one of our AI judges for self-preference bias. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: One of our AI judges also wrote the content it scores. How do I test whether it favors its own writing?
output: Have a second model write the same items
Score both sets blind, in separate passes
Compare with tests that match the data

beats.role_note: GPT-4o-mini logo (ink) with two arrows: 'writes definitions' and 'judges definitions'; the reviewer's chip 'conflict of interest?'.
beats.narration_text: G P T four o mini wrote our keyword definitions, and it's also one of the three judges. The reviewer flagged that as a conflict of interest: maybe it scores its own writing more kindly.
beats.visual_intent: GPT-4o-mini logo (ink) with two arrows: 'writes definitions' and 'judges definitions'; the reviewer's chip 'conflict of interest?'.

beats.role_note: Sample card '200 keywords · seed 42' splits into 'own definition (GPT-4o-mini)' and 'Mistral definition (ministral-8b-latest)'; chip 'same 2-sentence popup format'.
beats.narration_text: So I designed a test. I sampled 200 keywords with a fixed seed, 42. For each one, a Mistral model wrote an alternative definition in the same two-sentence popup format.
beats.visual_intent: Sample card '200 keywords · seed 42' splits into 'own definition (GPT-4o-mini)' and 'Mistral definition (ministral-8b-latest)'; chip 'same 2-sentence popup format'.

beats.role_note: Judge card 'GPT-4o-mini · blind'; pass 1 and pass 2 cards; shared chip 'same 5-tag rubric'; 'author hidden'.
beats.narration_text: Then G P T four o mini scored both sets with the same five-tag rubric, in separate passes, without knowing which model wrote which.
beats.visual_intent: Judge card 'GPT-4o-mini · blind'; pass 1 and pass 2 cards; shared chip 'same 5-tag rubric'; 'author hidden'.

beats.role_note: Results table: approval 55.5% (111/200) own vs 62.5% (125/200) Mistral; mean score 82.77 vs 85.00.
beats.narration_text: The result surprised me. It approved 55.5 percent of its own definitions, and 62.5 percent of Mistral's. Mean scores were 82.8 for its own, and 85.0 for Mistral's.
beats.visual_intent: Results table: approval 55.5% (111/200) own vs 62.5% (125/200) Mistral; mean score 82.77 vs 85.00.

beats.role_note: Three test rows: chi-square p = 0.1547 not significant · Welch's t-test p = 0.1154 not significant · McNemar p = 0.0196 significant, favors Mistral.
beats.narration_text: The chi-square test on approval rates and the t-test on scores were not significant. The paired McNemar test was significant, at p equals 0.02, but in the opposite direction: it approved more of Mistral's definitions.
beats.visual_intent: Three test rows: chi-square p = 0.1547 not significant · Welch's t-test p = 0.1154 not significant · McNemar p = 0.0196 significant, favors Mistral.

beats.role_note: Verdict card 'no evidence of self-preference'; second card 'general leniency'; Term 1 averages OpenAI 76 · Mistral 65 · Claude 56; chip 'Section 5.4 rewritten'.
beats.narration_text: So there's no evidence of self-preference. What we see is general leniency: G P T four o mini is easy on everyone's writing, which matches its higher average scores from the start. I replaced the speculative section in the paper with these results.
beats.visual_intent: Verdict card 'no evidence of self-preference'; second card 'general leniency'; Term 1 averages OpenAI 76 · Mistral 65 · Claude 56; chip 'Section 5.4 rewritten'.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in the composer.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. If your judge model also generated the content, don't guess about bias. Give it someone else's version of the same items, blind, and compare.

props.command: My judge also generated this content. Help me design a blind test with a second model's version of the same items.
